sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ kurumādhavasiṃhayoḥ anyonyaṃ kruddhayor ghoraṃ yathā dviradasiṃhayoḥ
english: Then a terrible battle broke out between those two lions, the Kuru and the Mādhava, each enraged against the other, like a duel between an elephant and a lion.

sanskrit: tataḥ pūrṇāyatotsṛṣṭaiḥ sātvataṃ yuddhadurmadam duryodhanaḥ pratyavidhyad daśabhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then Duryodhana struck the Sātvata, that warrior frenzied for battle, in return with ten sharp arrows loosed from a fully drawn bow.

sanskrit: taṃ sātyakiḥ pratyaviddhat tathaiva daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ pañcāśatā punaś cājau triṃśatā daśabhiś ca ha
english: Sātyaki struck him back likewise with ten arrows, and again in that fight with fifty, with thirty, and with ten more.

sanskrit: tasya saṃdadhataś ceṣūn saṃhiteṣuṃ ca kārmukam acchinat sātyakis tūrṇaṃ śaraiś caivābhyavīvṛṣat
english: As Duryodhana was fitting his shafts, Sātyaki swiftly cut apart his bow with its arrow already nocked, and rained his own shafts down upon him.

sanskrit: sa gāḍhaviddho vyathitaḥ pratyapāyād rathāntaram duryodhano mahārāja dāśārhaśarapīḍitaḥ
english: Pierced deep and shaken, O great king, Duryodhana, tormented by the arrows of the Dāśārha, withdrew to another chariot.

sanskrit: samāśvasya tu putras te sātyakiṃ punar abhyayāt visṛjann iṣujālāni yuyudhānarathaṃ prati
english: But once he had recovered, your son again advanced upon Sātyaki, loosing networks of arrows against the chariot of Yuyudhāna.

sanskrit: tathaiva sātyakir bāṇān duryodhanarathaṃ prati pratataṃ vyasṛjad rājaṃs tat saṃkulam avartata
english: And so Sātyaki too loosed his arrows in a steady stream against Duryodhana's chariot, O king, and a tumult of close fighting arose.

sanskrit: tatreṣubhiḥ kṣipyamāṇaiḥ patadbhiś ca samantataḥ agner iva mahākakṣe śabdaḥ samabhavan mahān
english: There, from the arrows hurled and falling on every side, a great roar arose, like fire raging through a vast thicket.

sanskrit: tatrābhyadhikam ālakṣya mādhavaṃ rathasattamam kṣipram abhyapatat karṇaḥ parīpsaṃs tanayaṃ tava
english: Seeing the Mādhava, that foremost of chariot-warriors, gaining the upper hand, Karṇa swiftly rushed in, eager to save your son.

sanskrit: na tu taṃ marṣayām āsa bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ abhyayāt tvaritaḥ karṇaṃ visṛjan sāyakān bahūn
english: But the mighty Bhīmasena would not endure this; he rushed swiftly upon Karṇa, loosing many shafts.

sanskrit: tasya karṇaḥ śitān bāṇān pratihanya hasann iva dhanuḥ śarāṃś ca ciccheda sūtaṃ cābhyahanac charaiḥ
english: Karṇa, as if laughing, beat back his sharp arrows, cut apart his bow and shafts, and struck down his charioteer with his own arrows.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu saṃkruddho gadām ādāya pāṇḍavaḥ dhvajaṃ dhanuś ca sūtaṃ ca saṃmamardāhave ripoḥ
english: But Bhīmasena the Pāṇḍava, enraged, took up his mace and in the battle crushed the banner, bow, and charioteer of his foe.

sanskrit: amṛṣyamāṇaḥ karṇas tu bhīmasenam ayudhyata vividhair iṣujālaiś ca nānāśastraiś ca saṃyuge
english: Unable to bear this, Karṇa fought against Bhīmasena in the encounter with manifold networks of arrows and with weapons of every kind.

sanskrit: saṃkule vartamāne tu rājā dharmasuto 'bravīt pāñcālānāṃ naravyāghrān matsyānāṃ ca nararṣabhān
english: While the press of battle raged on, the king, the son of Dharma, spoke to the tigers among men of the Pāñcālas and the bulls among men of the Matsyas:

sanskrit: ye naḥ prāṇāḥ śiro ye no ye no yodhā mahābalāḥ ta ete dhārtarāṣṭreṣu viṣaktāḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ
english: "Those who are our very breath, who are our head, our warriors of mighty strength — those bulls among men are now locked in struggle against the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra."

sanskrit: kiṃ tiṣṭhata yathā mūḍhāḥ sarve vigatacetasaḥ tatra gacchata yatraite yudhyante māmakā rathāḥ
english: "Why do you stand here, all of you, like bewildered men robbed of your wits? Go there, where these chariot-warriors of mine are fighting!"

sanskrit: kṣatradharmaṃ puraskṛtya sarva eva gatajvarāḥ jayanto vadhyamānā vā gatim iṣṭāṃ gamiṣyatha
english: "Setting the warrior's duty foremost, every one of you with your fevered fear cast off — whether conquering or slain, you shall attain the destiny you desire."

sanskrit: jitvā ca bahubhir yajñair yakṣyadhvaṃ bhūridakṣiṇaiḥ hatā vā devasād bhūtvā lokān prāpsyatha puṣkalān
english: "And conquering, you shall offer many sacrifices with abundant gifts; or slain, having passed into the company of the gods, you shall attain bountiful worlds."

sanskrit: te rājñā coditā vīrā yotsyamānā mahārathāḥ caturdhā vahinīṃ kṛtvā tvaritā droṇam abhyayuḥ
english: Urged on by the king, those heroes, the great chariot-warriors eager to fight, formed their host into four divisions and swiftly advanced upon Droṇa.

sanskrit: pāñcālās tv ekato droṇam abhyaghnan bahubhiḥ śaraiḥ bhīmasenapurogāś ca ekataḥ paryavārayan
english: From one side the Pāñcālas assailed Droṇa with many arrows, and from another those led by Bhīmasena hemmed him in.

sanskrit: āsaṃs tu pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ trayo 'jihmā mahārathāḥ yamau ca bhīmasenaś ca prākrośanta dhanaṃjayam
english: Among the sons of Pāṇḍu there were three unswerving great chariot-warriors — the twins and Bhīmasena — and they cried out to Dhanaṃjaya:

sanskrit: abhidravārjuna kṣipraṃ kurūn droṇād apānuda tata enaṃ haniṣyanti pāñcālā hatarakṣiṇam
english: "Charge swiftly, Arjuna! Drive the Kurus away from Droṇa, and then the Pāñcālas will slay him, his protector removed."

sanskrit: kauraveyāṃs tataḥ pārthaḥ sahasā samupādravat pāñcālān eva tu droṇo dhṛṣṭadyumnapurogamān
english: Then Pārtha rushed suddenly upon the Kauravas, while Droṇa fell upon the Pāñcālas led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: pāñcālānāṃ tato droṇo 'py akarot kadanaṃ mahat yathā kruddho raṇe śakro dānavānāṃ kṣayaṃ purā
english: Then Droṇa too wrought great slaughter among the Pāñcālas, as Śakra in his wrath had once wrought the destruction of the Dānavas in battle.

sanskrit: droṇāstreṇa mahārāja vadhyamānāḥ pare yudhi nātrasanta raṇe droṇāt sattvavanto mahārathāḥ
english: Though slaughtered by Droṇa's weapon in the fight, O great king, those great chariot-warriors of resolute spirit did not flinch from Droṇa in the battle.

sanskrit: vadhyamānā mahārāja pāñcālāḥ sṛñjayās tathā droṇam evābhyayur yuddhe mohayanto mahāratham
english: Though being slaughtered, O great king, the Pāñcālas and the Sṛñjayas pressed on against Droṇa in the fight, bewildering that great chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tūtsādyamānānāṃ pāñcālānāṃ samantataḥ abhavad bhairavo nādo vadhyatāṃ śaraśaktibhiḥ
english: As those Pāñcālas were being cut down on every side, slain by arrows and lances, a fearful cry arose among them.

sanskrit: vadhyamāneṣu saṃgrāme pāñcāleṣu mahātmanā udīryamāṇe droṇāstre pāṇḍavān bhayam āviśat
english: As the Pāñcālas were being slaughtered in the battle by that great soul, and as Droṇa's weapon raged on, fear entered into the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvāśvanarasaṃghānāṃ vipulaṃ ca kṣayaṃ yudhi pāṇḍaveyā mahārāja nāśaṃsur vijayaṃ tadā
english: Seeing the vast destruction of their hosts of horses and men in the fight, the Pāṇḍavas, O great king, then despaired of victory.

sanskrit: kaccid droṇo na naḥ sarvān kṣapayet paramāstravit samiddhaḥ śiśirāpāye dahan kakṣam ivānalaḥ
english: "Will not Droṇa, master of the supreme weapons, destroy us all — like a blazing fire at winter's end consuming dry brushwood?"

sanskrit: na cainaṃ saṃyuge kaś cit samarthaḥ prativīkṣitum na cainam arjuno jātu pratiyudhyeta dharmavit
english: "None in battle is able even to look him in the face, nor would Arjuna, who knows what is right, ever fight against him."

sanskrit: trastān kuntīsutān dṛṣṭvā droṇasāyakapīḍitān matimāñ śreyase yuktaḥ keśavo 'rjunam abravīt
english: Seeing the sons of Kuntī terrified and tormented by Droṇa's arrows, the wise Keśava, intent upon their welfare, spoke to Arjuna:

sanskrit: naiṣa yuddhena saṃgrāme jetuṃ śakyaḥ kathaṃ cana api vṛtrahaṇā yuddhe rathayūthapayūthapaḥ
english: "This commander of the leaders of chariot-bands can in no way be conquered in open battle, not even by the Slayer of Vṛtra himself."

sanskrit: āsthīyatāṃ jaye yogo dharmam utsṛjya pāṇḍava yathā vaḥ saṃyuge sarvān na hanyād rukmavāhanaḥ
english: "For the sake of victory, O Pāṇḍava, let some stratagem be employed, setting aside strict righteousness, so that he of the golden chariot may not slay you all in the encounter."

sanskrit: aśvatthāmni hate naiṣa yudhyed iti matir mama taṃ hataṃ saṃyuge kaś cid asmai śaṃsatu mānavaḥ
english: "It is my belief that, were Aśvatthāman slain, he would fight no more. Let some man announce to him that his son has been slain in battle."

sanskrit: etan nārocayad rājan kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ anye tv arocayan sarve kṛcchreṇa tu yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: This did not please the son of Kuntī, Dhanaṃjaya, O king; but all the others approved of it, and Yudhiṣṭhira only with great reluctance.

sanskrit: tato bhīmo mahābāhur anīke sve mahāgajam jaghāna gadayā rājann aśvatthāmānam ity uta
english: Then mighty-armed Bhīma, within his own ranks, slew with his mace a great elephant named Aśvatthāman, O king.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu savrīḍam upetya droṇam āhave aśvatthāmā hata iti śabdam uccaiś cakāra ha
english: Then Bhīmasena, somewhat abashed, approached Droṇa in the battle and cried aloud, "Aśvatthāman is slain!"

sanskrit: aśvatthāmeti hi gajaḥ khyāto nāmnā hato 'bhavat kṛtvā manasi taṃ bhīmo mithyā vyāhṛtavāṃs tadā
english: It was the elephant known by the name Aśvatthāman that had been slain; keeping that in his mind, Bhīma then spoke falsely.

sanskrit: bhīmasenavacaḥ śrutvā droṇas tat param apriyam manasā sannagātro 'bhūd yathā saikatam ambhasi
english: Hearing Bhīmasena's words, that most unwelcome news, Droṇa grew limp in his limbs in spirit, like a bank of sand in water.

sanskrit: śaṅkamānaḥ sa tan mithyā vīryajñaḥ svasutasya vai hataḥ sa iti ca śrutvā naiva dhairyād akampata
english: Suspecting it to be false, for he knew his own son's valor, and hearing "He is slain," he did not waver from his steadfastness.

sanskrit: sa labdhvā cetanāṃ droṇaḥ kṣaṇenaiva samāśvasat anucintyātmanaḥ putram aviṣahyam arātibhiḥ
english: Regaining his composure, Droṇa recovered himself in but a moment, reflecting that his own son was invincible to his foes.

sanskrit: sa pārṣatam abhidrutya jighāṃsur mṛtyum ātmanaḥ avākirat sahasreṇa tīkṣṇānāṃ kaṅkapatriṇām
english: Rushing upon the son of Pṛṣata, seeking to slay him who was his own death, he covered him with a thousand sharp heron-feathered arrows.

sanskrit: taṃ vai viṃśatisāhasrāḥ pāñcālānāṃ nararṣabhāḥ tathā carantaṃ saṃgrāme sarvato vyakirañ śaraiḥ
english: As he ranged thus through the battle, twenty thousand of those bulls among men of the Pāñcālas showered him with arrows from every side.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāduṣkarod droṇo brāhmam astraṃ paraṃtapaḥ vadhāya teṣāṃ śūrāṇāṃ pāñcālānām amarṣitaḥ
english: Then Droṇa, scorcher of foes, in his fury brought forth the weapon of Brahmā for the destruction of those heroic Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: tato vyarocata droṇo vinighnan sarvasomakān śirāṃsy apātayac cāpi pāñcālānāṃ mahāmṛdhe tathaiva parighākārān bāhūn kanakabhūṣaṇān
english: Then Droṇa blazed forth, striking down all the Somakas; in that great battle he made the heads of the Pāñcālas fall, and likewise their arms, shaped like iron clubs and adorned with gold.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ samare bhāradvājena pārthivāḥ medinyām anvakīryanta vātanunnā iva drumāḥ
english: Those kings, slaughtered in battle by the son of Bharadvāja, were strewn upon the earth like trees felled by the wind.

sanskrit: kuñjarāṇāṃ ca patatāṃ hayaughānāṃ ca bhārata agamyarūpā pṛthivī māṃsaśoṇitakardamā
english: With elephants and floods of horses falling, O descendant of Bharata, the earth, a mire of flesh and blood, became impassable to behold.

sanskrit: hatvā viṃśatisāhasrān pāñcālānāṃ rathavrajān atiṣṭhad āhave droṇo vidhūmo 'gnir iva jvalan
english: Having slain twenty thousand bands of Pāñcāla chariot-warriors, Droṇa stood in the battle blazing like a smokeless fire.

sanskrit: tathaiva ca punaḥ kruddho bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān vasudānasya bhallena śiraḥ kāyād apāharat
english: And so once more the mighty son of Bharadvāja in his wrath struck off the head of Vasudāna from his body with a broad-headed shaft.

sanskrit: punaḥ pañcaśatān matsyān ṣaṭsahasrāṃś ca sṛñjayān hastinām ayutaṃ hatvā jaghānāśvāyutaṃ punaḥ
english: Again, slaying five hundred Matsyas and six thousand Sṛñjayas and ten thousand elephants, he then slew ten thousand horses as well.

sanskrit: kṣatriyāṇām abhāvāya dṛṣṭvā droṇam avasthitam ṛṣayo 'bhyāgamaṃs tūrṇaṃ havyavāhapurogamāḥ
english: Seeing Droṇa set upon the annihilation of the warriors, the seers swiftly drew near, led by the Bearer of Oblations.

sanskrit: viśvāmitro jamadagnir bhāradvājo 'tha gautamaḥ vasiṣṭhaḥ kaśyapo 'triś ca brahmalokaṃ ninīṣavaḥ
english: Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni, Bharadvāja, and Gautama, Vasiṣṭha, Kaśyapa, and Atri, desiring to lead him to the world of Brahmā —

sanskrit: sikatāḥ pṛśnayo gargā bālakhilyā marīcipāḥ bhṛgavo 'ṅgirasaś caiva sūkṣmāś cānye maharṣayaḥ
english: the Sikatas, the Pṛśnis, the Gargas, the Bālakhilyas, the Marīcipas, the Bhṛgus and the Aṅgirases, and other subtle great seers —

sanskrit: ta enam abruvan sarve droṇam āhavaśobhinam adharmataḥ kṛtaṃ yuddhaṃ samayo nidhanasya te
english: all these said to Droṇa, resplendent in battle: "Unrighteously has this war been waged; the hour of your death has come."

sanskrit: nyasyāyudhaṃ raṇe droṇa sametyāsmān avasthitān nātaḥ krūrataraṃ karma punaḥ kartuṃ tvam arhasi
english: "Lay down your weapon in the battle, O Droṇa, and come to join us who stand here. You ought not again to do a deed more cruel than this."

sanskrit: vedavedāṅgaviduṣaḥ satyadharmaparasya ca brāhmaṇasya viśeṣeṇa tavaitan nopapadyate
english: "For you who know the Vedas and their auxiliaries, who are devoted to truth and righteousness, and a Brāhmaṇa above all — this is unbecoming."

sanskrit: nyasyāyudham amogheṣo tiṣṭha vartmani śāśvate paripūrṇaś ca kālas te vastuṃ loke 'dya mānuṣe
english: "Lay down your weapon, O you whose shafts never miss; stand upon the eternal path. Your time for dwelling in this human world is now fulfilled."

sanskrit: iti teṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā bhīmasenavacaś ca tat dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca saṃprekṣya raṇe sa vimanābhavat
english: Hearing these words of theirs, and those words of Bhīmasena, and beholding Dhṛṣṭadyumna in the battle, he became downcast in spirit.

sanskrit: sa dahyamāno vyathitaḥ kuntīputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram ahataṃ vā hataṃ veti papraccha sutam ātmanaḥ
english: Burning within and troubled, he asked Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī, whether his own son was unslain or slain.

sanskrit: sthirā buddhir hi droṇasya na pārtho vakṣyate 'nṛtam trayāṇām api lokānām aiśvaryārthe kathaṃ cana
english: For Droṇa was firm in his conviction that Pārtha would not speak a falsehood, not even for the lordship of all three worlds.

sanskrit: tasmāt taṃ paripapraccha nānyaṃ kaṃ cid viśeṣataḥ tasmiṃs tasya hi satyāśā bālyāt prabhṛti pāṇḍave
english: Therefore he questioned him in particular and no other; for in that Pāṇḍava his hope of truth had rested from boyhood.

sanskrit: tato niṣpāṇḍavām urvīṃ kariṣyantaṃ yudhāṃ patim droṇaṃ jñātvā dharmarājaṃ govindo vyathito 'bravīt
english: Then, knowing that Droṇa, that lord of warriors, was about to make the earth bereft of the Pāṇḍavas, Govinda, troubled, spoke to the King of Righteousness:

sanskrit: yady ardhadivasaṃ droṇo yudhyate manyum āsthitaḥ satyaṃ bravīmi te senā vināśaṃ samupaiṣyati
english: "If Droṇa, possessed by wrath, fights for half a day longer, I tell you truly: your army will go to its destruction."

sanskrit: sa bhavāṃs trātu no droṇāt satyāj jyāyo 'nṛtaṃ bhavet anṛtaṃ jīvitasyārthe vadan na spṛśyate 'nṛtaiḥ
english: "Therefore save us from Droṇa: a falsehood here may be greater than truth. He who utters an untruth to save a life is not tainted by untruths."

sanskrit: tayoḥ saṃvadator evaṃ bhīmaseno 'bravīd idam śrutvaiva taṃ mahārāja vadhopāyaṃ mahātmanaḥ
english: As the two were thus speaking together, Bhīmasena, having heard of that device for slaying the great soul, said this, O great king:

sanskrit: gāhamānasya te senāṃ mālavasyendravarmaṇaḥ aśvatthāmeti vikhyāto gajaḥ śakragajopamaḥ
english: "As I was plunging into your host, there was an elephant named Aśvatthāman, like unto the elephant of Śakra, belonging to Indravarman the Mālava;"

sanskrit: nihato yudhi vikramya tato 'haṃ droṇam abruvam aśvatthāmā hato brahman nivartasvāhavād iti
english: "him I valiantly slew in the fight, and then I said to Droṇa: 'Aśvatthāman is slain, O Brāhmaṇa; withdraw from the battle!'"

sanskrit: nūnaṃ nāśraddadhad vākyam eṣa me puruṣarṣabhaḥ sa tvaṃ govindavākyāni mānayasva jayaiṣiṇaḥ
english: "Surely this bull among men did not believe my word. So now do you honor the words of Govinda, who desires victory."

sanskrit: droṇāya nihataṃ śaṃsa rājañ śāradvatīsutam tvayokto naiṣa yudhyeta jātu rājan dvijarṣabhaḥ satyavān hi nṛloke 'smin bhavān khyāto janādhipa
english: "Declare to Droṇa, O king, that the son of Śāradvatī is slain. Told so by you, this bull among the twice-born would surely fight no more, O king; for in this world of men you are renowned as truthful, O ruler of peoples."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā kṛṣṇavākyapracoditaḥ bhāvitvāc ca mahārāja vaktuṃ samupacakrame
english: Hearing those words of his, urged on by the words of Kṛṣṇa, and because of what was destined to be, O great king, Yudhiṣṭhira set himself to speak.

sanskrit: tam atathyabhaye magno jaye sakto yudhiṣṭhiraḥ avyaktam abravīd rājan hataḥ kuñjara ity uta
english: Sunk in dread of the untruth yet clinging to victory, Yudhiṣṭhira said indistinctly, O king, "He is slain" — and under his breath, "the elephant."

sanskrit: tasya pūrvaṃ rathaḥ pṛthvyāś caturaṅgula uttaraḥ babhūvaivaṃ tu tenokte tasya vāhāspṛśan mahīm
english: Before this his chariot had stood four finger-breadths above the earth; but when he had spoken thus, his horses touched the ground.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhirāt tu tad vākyaṃ śrutvā droṇo mahārathaḥ putravyasanasaṃtapto nirāśo jīvite 'bhavat
english: Hearing those words from Yudhiṣṭhira, Droṇa, the great chariot-warrior, scorched by grief at his son's calamity, lost all hope of life.

sanskrit: āgaskṛtam ivātmānaṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām ṛṣivākyaṃ ca manvānaḥ śrutvā ca nihataṃ sutam
english: Deeming himself an offender against the great-souled Pāṇḍavas, and pondering the words of the seers, and having heard his son was slain —

sanskrit: vicetāḥ paramodvigno dhṛṣṭadyumnam avekṣya ca yoddhuṃ nāśaknuvad rājan yathāpūrvam ariṃdama
english: bewildered and stricken with the deepest dismay, and looking upon Dhṛṣṭadyumna, he was no longer able to fight as before, O king, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā paramodvignaṃ śokopahatacetasam pāñcālarājasya suto dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ samādravat
english: Seeing him utterly distraught, his mind overwhelmed by grief, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the son of the Pāñcāla king, rushed upon him.

sanskrit: ya iṣṭvā manujendreṇa drupadena mahāmakhe labdho droṇavināśāya samiddhād dhavyavāhanāt
english: He who, when the lord of men Drupada had sacrificed at the great rite, had been obtained for Droṇa's destruction from the blazing Bearer of Oblations —

sanskrit: sa dhanur jaitram ādāya ghoraṃ jaladanisvanam dṛḍhajyam ajaraṃ divyaṃ śarāṃś cāśīviṣopamān
english: he, taking up his victorious bow, terrible, roaring like a thundercloud, firm-stringed, undecaying, and divine, and arrows like venomous serpents —

sanskrit: saṃdadhe kārmuke tasmiñ śaram āśīviṣopamam droṇaṃ jighāṃsuḥ pāñcālyo mahājvālam ivānalam
english: the Pāñcāla, seeking to slay Droṇa, fitted to that bow a shaft like a venomous serpent, like a vast-flaming fire.
